rationale: Jesus introduces this quotation with his own citation wording, "It is written" (4:4), and quotes Deuteronomy 8:3's own conclusion to the manna narrative. Checked directly against both texts as shipped in this app, the wording differs in two traceable ways: Deuteronomy's own clause sits inside a purpose statement ("so that you might understand that man does not live on bread alone"), where Matthew's quotation stands as a freestanding assertion ("Man shall not live on bread alone"); and Matthew's Greek text reads "the mouth of God" (theou), which matches the Septuagint's own wording for this verse exactly -- the Septuagint itself reads theou here, not the more usual kyrios for the Hebrew divine name -- so the gap from this app's English Deuteronomy rendering ("the mouth of the LORD") traces to a Septuagint translation choice already present before Matthew, not a change Matthew introduces. The label stays explicit because the citation formula and the quoted content are both unambiguous, not because every word matches letter for letter.
